title: Beni Mellal city and foothills on 22 Jun 2026
summary: On 22 Jun 2026 the radar shows Beni Mellal city and its foothills inside a 6 km circle, where built-up land covers 12.2% and trees, shrub and rugged slopes 52.5%. No flag applies to this date, and 100.0% of the circle has data.

sections.heading: What the radar shows here
sections.text: Built-up land is by far the brightest surface, with HH at 5.57 dB against a circle mean of -2.3 dB. HV is much lower everywhere: the circle mean is -13.73 dB, and even built-up land reaches only -10.7 dB in HV.

sections.heading: Terrain types and what they mean
sections.text: Built-up land, 13.75 km2, has an HV:HH ratio of -16.27 dB, the lowest of all types, because walls and the street beside them bounce the pulse straight back in HH. Trees, shrub and rugged slopes, 59.32 km2, give HV of -12.91 dB from leaves and branches. Rough dry ground and fields cover 27.3% at -10.9 dB in HH. Changing fields, 4.8%, sit at -15.76 dB in HV.

sections.heading: Data quality notes
sections.text: No flag applies on this date. The circle is seen from one track only, so slopes facing away from the radar can fall in shadow and look darker than they are. Possible cause of some very bright points outside the city: farm buildings and walls; the optical photo would show them.
